SO FAR AS THE PETITIONER IS CONCERNED, WHICH IS PRODUCED AS ANNEXURE-F AND ETC.,
 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER Sri. R.Srinivasa Gowda, learned AGA accepts notice on behalf of respondent No.1; Sri.H.L.Pradeep Kumar, learned Panel counsel accepts notice on behalf of respondent Nos.2 & 3.
2.

The learned AGA and also the learned Panel counsel for the respondent-KIADB are broadly in agreement that the fact matrix of this writ petition is substantially similar to the one in W.P.Nos.39611- 39612/2016 (LA-KIADB) disposed of by the Coordinate Bench of this Court vide judgment dated 16.09.2016.

The paragraphs 2 & 3 of the said decision reads as under:-
"2. Section 29(2) of 'KIAD Act', provides for determination of compensation by way of agreement.

Therefore, petitioners are entitled to such a consideration since it is stated that by agreement, petitioners would be entitled to a better price as Sri R Chenraj Jain vs The State Of Karnataka on 13 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36842967/
2 compensation instead of a determination by way of a general award.

sentences.text: In addition, it is stated that there would be a finality to the acquisition proceedings and also for settlement of compensation since petitioners would be disentitled to challenge the same and to seek for higher market value/compensation.
Therefore, there is a need to interfere with the general award at Annexure-F in so far as petitioners are concerned.
3. In the circumstances, these petitions are allowed.
General award at Annexure-F on so far as it relates to petitioners, is quashed.

A direction shall ensue to the third respondent- Special Land Acquisition Officer, KIADB, to consider the case of the petitioners for determination of compensation by way of agreement under Section 29(2) of the KIAD Act, to be complied with as expeditiously as possible within eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.

It is made clear that this order is applicable if there is no dispute to title to the immovable property acquired and if there is one, then the general award in so far as petitioners are concerned will stand restored, until the dispute is resolved in favour of the petitioners.
The third respondent is permitted to withdraw the award amount in relation to the aforesaid land, if deposited in the Civil Court.
No costs."

3. There is an assurance, both from the side of the respondent-Government and the respondent KIADB that petitioner's representation shall be considered in terms of aforementioned paragraphs 2 & 3 for treating the said acquisition as the one made with the consent of the land owner for the purpose of payment of compensation within a reasonable period under Section 29(2) of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act, 1966.

In view of the above, this Writ Petition succeeds in terms of the decision cited above; a Writ of Certiorari issues quashing the impugned award dated 16.7.2022 (Annexure-F) only so far as it relates to the lands of the petitioner for the purpose of determination & payment of compensation as if the award is by agreement under Section 29 (2) of the Act, leaving the vested title of the land with the respondent-KIADB, otherwise unaffected.
No costs.
